newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds up, some yield spreads tighter.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds up, some yield spreads tighter.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities rode the coattails of a Treasury market rally during much of Friday's session, but some discount coupons pulled ahead late in the day to tighten their yield spreads modestly.
Pass-throughs were up 4/32 to 24/32 overall, with the best performance concentrated in smaller-coupon Ginnie Mae paper.
"We saw decent buying in Ginnies," one New York trader said. "Retail activity picked up a little today."
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper was up 15/32 at 99-18/32, yielding 97 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were up 13/32 as well, at 99-20/32 and 99-24/32, respectively.
Five-year Treasuries were up 11/32 at 6.52 percent, and 10-year notes were up 15/32 at 6.67 percent.
The credit-market improvement developed in Europe overnight as investors digested comments made by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Thursday.

In a New York speech, Greenspan said the central bank would need to act if economic strength shows signs it will persist, but he added that economic conditions now are different from those that provoked severe monetary tightening in 1994.

Analysts initially saw the comments as an indication the Fed may stand pat it its May 20 policy meeting. But a Reuters poll showed 19 of 26 economists still expect a 25-basis-point rate hike later this month.
